newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Horse Racing-HK charges five in betting scandal.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-HK charges five in betting scandal.

text.p: Five people were charged on Tuesday with offences linked to taking illegal bets in Hong Kong's worst horse racing scandal, but a court set them free on bail.
Two of the accused were Malaysian citizens, according to papers presented in the court at a hearing open to the media.
All five were charged with engaging in illegal bookmaking, and all five pleaded not guilty. They will appear in court again on May 16.
The Malaysians were Yong Seng-Chen and Liew Siew-cheong. The other three were Hong Kong residents Chan Hung-yip, Kam Tat-Fai and Ching Fuk-hung. Their occupations were not stated.
The Malaysians were released on bail of HK$750,000 (US$96,154) each in cash. The Hong Kong defendants were released on bail of HK$100,000 each.

The charges stem from the biggest race fixing and illegal betting scandal on Hong Kong's race courses, in which 37 people have been hauled in for questioning in the past two days. None of the other 32 has been charged so far.
